title: English Opening: the ideas
line: The c-pawn goes first, a bishop watches the long diagonal, and the queenside pawns march.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c2 two squares. From the side it fights for the center square d5.

also.e2e4: That is the most played first move, the king pawn opening. This lesson starts with the side pawn.
also.d2d4: That is the queen pawn opening, also sound. This lesson starts with the side pawn.
also.g1f3: That is the knight first, often a Réti Opening. This lesson starts with the side pawn.

steps.after: This is the English Opening. Black takes the center with its king pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It watches d5 too.

also.g2g3: Opening the diagonal for the bishop first is sound too. This lesson brings the knight out first.
also.g1f3: That attacks the pawn on e5, also sound. This lesson brings the other knight out first.

steps.text: Move the pawn on g2 one square. It opens the long diagonal for your bishop.

also.g1f3: That leads to the Four Knights setups, also sound. This lesson opens the diagonal first.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. It aims at the center and at the queenside.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It keeps the center closed and frees your other bishop.
Put the rook behind the pawn on b2. White plays on the queenside, where the bishop on g2 looks.
steps.after: Black pushes a pawn to slow down your pawn on b2.

steps.text: Move the pawn on a2 one square. It backs up the pawn push that comes next.
Push the pawn on b2 two squares. The pawns roll forward on the queenside, with the rook behind them.
steps.after: White takes space on the queenside while the center stays closed.

summary: The side pawn fights for the center, the bishop watches the long diagonal, and the queenside pawns move up.
